The proposed answer of 4 is correct, though one step in the reasoning is flawed.

The series has first term 4 and common ratio 3/a, so it converges only when a > 3. Its sum is 4a/(a−3). The smallest integer allowed is a = 4, which gives a sum of 16/1 = 16 = 4², a perfect square. No smaller positive integer gives a convergent series, so 4 is the smallest valid value.

The flawed step is the claim that 4a/(a−3) is a perfect square only if 4a and a−3 are both perfect squares. That is not a valid equivalence. Also, the discussion of a = 1 and a = 2 is irrelevant, because those values make the series diverge. These errors do not change the result.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
